related_questions.question: What are the symptoms of the rotavirus?

text_blocks.snippet: Rotavirus infection typically causes gastroenteritis with symptoms like vomiting and watery diarrhea, often accompanied by fever and abdominal pain. Dehydration is a common complication, especially in infants, and can manifest as decreased urination, dry mouth, and unusual sleepiness. Symptoms usually appear within two days of exposure and can last for several days.
snippet_highlighted_words: vomiting and watery diarrhea, often accompanied by fever and abdominal pain

list.snippet: Fever: Usually subsides within the first couple of days.
Vomiting: May be brief.
Watery diarrhea: Can be frequent and last for three to eight days.
Abdominal pain: May occur.
Loss of appetite: Can be a symptom.
Dehydration: A serious concern, especially for infants. Symptoms include:
Decreased urination
Dry mouth and throat
Feeling dizzy when standing up
Crying with few or no tears
Unusual sleepiness or fussiness
Sunken eyes
Sunken fontanelle (soft spot on the head) in babies
Lack of tears when crying
Inability to keep down liquids: Especially for 24 hours.
Diarrhea lasting more than two days:
Blood in vomit or stool:
High fever: Particularly in infants (under 6 months) or for more than 24 hours in older children.
Signs of dehydration: Excessive thirst, dry mouth, little to no urination, severe weakness, dizziness upon standing.
Severe stomach pain:
Lethargy or extreme sleepiness:

related_questions.question: How serious is rotavirus?
related_questions.snippet: Most children recover from rotavirus without long-term health effects. Symptoms last about a week. If your child becomes dehydrated, it could lead to serious complications and even death. Call your healthcare provider right away if your child shows symptoms of rotavirus.

text_blocks.snippet: Rotavirus is contagious for several days before symptoms appear and can continue to be contagious for up to two weeks after symptoms resolve. Infected individuals shed the virus in their stool, and it can be transmitted through various routes like fecal-oral contact and contaminated objects.

text_blocks.snippet: Rotavirus, not "rota disease," is a highly contagious virus that primarily affects infants and young children, causing gastroenteritis (inflammation of the stomach and intestines). Symptoms include severe diarrhea, vomiting, fever, and dehydration. While it can affect adults, it's generally more severe in young children.
snippet_highlighted_words: a highly contagious virus that primarily affects infants and young children, causing gastroenteritis (inflammation of the stomach and intestines)

list.snippet: Diarrhea: Often severe and watery.
Vomiting: Can be persistent and make it difficult to keep fluids down.
Fever: Can be present.

Dehydration: A serious concern, especially in young children, due to fluid loss from diarrhea and vomiting. Symptoms of dehydration include excessive thirst, dry mouth, decreased urination, dizziness, and lethargy.
Other: Loss of appetite, fussiness, and crying without tears.

text_blocks.snippet: Rotavirus is easily spread through the fecal-oral route, meaning it can be passed from person to person through contact with infected stool. It can also be spread through contaminated surfaces, food, or water. Outbreaks are common in daycare centers and schools.

list.snippet: No specific medication: Antibiotics and antivirals are not effective against rotavirus.
Focus on rehydration: The main goal is to prevent or treat dehydration by ensuring the child drinks plenty of fluids. Oral rehydration solutions (ORS) are often recommended.
Medical attention: In severe cases, especially if dehydration is severe, hospitalization for intravenous (IV) fluids may be necessary.

list.title: Rotavirus vaccine:
list.snippet: The most effective way to prevent rotavirus infection is through vaccination. Two vaccines are available in the U.S. and are given orally to infants.

list.title: Good hygiene:
list.snippet: Frequent handwashing, especially after using the toilet and before handling food, can help prevent the spread of the virus.

list.title: Sanitation:
list.snippet: Maintaining proper sanitation in places like daycare centers and schools is also important.
